text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young adult male presenting with aggressive behavior, altered mental status, and autonomic dysregulation. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you consumed any substances today?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient's roommates report that he has been displaying increasingly aggressive and unusual behavior. They mention that he has been under significant stress due to final exams and has become more reclusive. Earlier this evening, he exhibited extreme irritability, yelled at his computer, broke it, and then spent several hours at the gym.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP)

Your description of stress, reclusiveness, extreme irritability, and specifically the intense urge to exercise (spending hours at the gym) in the context of aggressive behavior and altered mental status is highly suggestive of an acute porphyric attack. The "gym" activity likely represents the characteristic restlessness and muscle weakness common in this condition. I need to confirm if you have any history of abdominal pain or dark urine, and I will order a urine porphobilinogen test to confirm.

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Porphobilinogen
